message.content:
**Famous 19th‑century dancers**

| Name | Nationality | Notable contributions |
|------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish/Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1879) | Italian | Developed the “Blasis system,” a foundational method for ballet technique. |
| **Carl Maria von Weber** (1786–1826) | German | Composer of *Der Freischütz*; his music influenced many dance productions. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Renowned for her virtuoso technique and dramatic stage presence. |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850–1928) | Italian | Created the Cecchetti method, still taught worldwide. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of *Swan Lake*, *The Nutcracker*, and *Sleeping Beauty*. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though born in the late 19th century, she became a leading ballerina in the early 20th. |
| **John Laird** (1840–1907) | British | Influential in the development of modern dance in Britain. |
| **George Balanchine** (1904–1983) | Russian-born | Though active mainly in the 20th century, he was trained in the 19th‑century Russian ballet tradition. |
| **Jean Coralli** (1796–1868) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle* (1841). |

These dancers were central figures in the evolution of ballet and other dance forms during the 19th century, shaping technique, choreography, and performance standards that continue to influence dancers today.
